title: Sheaf frames realizing the affine differential column
statement: Let W be a scheme, U an affine open, m a natural number, d in Γ(W,U)^m, and K a strictly perfect cochain complex on the localized module site over U [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Given section bases e0:Γ(K^0) ≃ Γ(W,U) and e1:Γ(K^1) ≃ Γ(W,U)^m identifying the section differential with a ↦ a d, there exist sheaf isomorphisms q0:A(K^0) ≅ O_U and q1:A(K^1) ≅ O_U^(ULift(Fin m)), where A is the open-site equivalence of [def-sc-picard-ordinary-model-cycles]. The column obtained by conjugating A(K.d 0 1) with these frames and evaluating its global section map at 1 has i-th entry U.topIso.inv(d i). No pullback morphism, residue field or cycle condition occurs.

source.place: Tag 0BF2, finite-free complex calculation; finite-projective module algebra

proof.text: Maps from the unit sheaf are sections at the terminal object. Maps from a free sheaf, and hence from any retract of it, are determined by their terminal section maps.

Send the free coordinate generators to the inverse images under the given section basis. The resulting sheaf map is bijective on terminal sections. Construct its inverse by lifting the generators of a free sheaf of which the term is a retract and composing with the retract inclusion. Terminal-section extensionality proves both inverse identities.

Apply this construction to e0 and e1. Transport the isomorphisms through the open-site equivalence, which preserves the unit, free coproducts and coordinate projections. Evaluate hd at one and transport the coefficients using U.topIso inverse. This also covers m=0 and requires no affine tilde equivalence.

lean.statement: theorem picard_ordinary_affine_differential_frames (W : Scheme.{v}) (U : W.Opens) (_hU : IsAffineOpen U) (m : ℕ) (d : Fin m → Γ(W, U)) (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{v} ((moduleRings W.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ) (hK : IsStrictlyPerfect W U K) (e0 : (K.X 0).val.obj (.op (Over.mk (𝟙 U))) ≃ₗ[Γ(W, U)] Γ(W, U)) (e1 : (K.X 1).val.obj (.op (Over.mk (𝟙 U))) ≃ₗ[Γ(W, U)] (Fin m → Γ(W, U))) (hd : ∀ a : Γ(W, U), e1 ((K.d 0 1).val.app (.op (Over.mk (𝟙 U))) (e0.symm a)) = a • d) : ∃ (q0 : (Modules.overEquiv U).functor.obj (K.X 0) ≅ Modules.unit U.toScheme) (q1 : (Modules.overEquiv U).functor.obj (K.X 1) ≅ SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{v} (Fin m))), ∀ i : Fin m, Modules.freeSectionsEquiv (ULift.{v} (Fin m)) (Modules.Hom.app (q0.inv ≫ (Modules.overEquiv U).functor.map (K.d 0 1) ≫ q1.hom) ⊤ (1 : Γ(U.toScheme, ⊤))) ⟨i⟩ = U.topIso.inv (d i)
